data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories inevitably smuggles induction back into Popper's system because the very concept of a 'severe test' presupposes the stability of natural laws and experimental conditions, an inductive assumption Popper explicitly sought to avoid.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If severity can be defined purely syntactically or logically without reference to empirical stability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the failure of a test can be treated as a timeless logical contradiction independent of temporal context.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Hidden Induction via Severity: A test is only 'severe' if the outcome was improbable given the background knowledge.
